column2: Chop the onion finely; chop the carrot small; wash the lentils.
Melt the butter in a pan and soften the onion for 3 minutes.
Add the lentils, carrot and water and bring to the boil; skim off the foam.
Cook over low heat for 25 minutes until the lentils break down.
Serve with lemon and bread.
Whisk the apple, egg, yoghurt and honey.
Add the flour, baking powder and cinnamon and mix just until combined.
Honey may only be given to children who have turned 1.
Knead the minced chicken, vegetables, oats and egg; leave for 10 minutes and wash your hands.
With wet hands, make walnut-sized flat patties and arrange on the tray.
Melt the butter in a pan and stir the tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add the carrot and boiled beans and stir for 2 minutes.
Add the water; cook covered over low heat for 20 minutes.
Mash the beans lightly and serve with rice.
Add yoghurt on the side.
Blend the yoghurt, strawberries and banana until smooth.
Pour into ice lolly moulds and insert the sticks.
Freeze for at least 5 hours.
Hold the mould under warm water for a few seconds to release.
Whisk the egg, flour and milk until smooth; add the courgette.
Spread the crepe with curd cheese and roll up.
Boil the potatoes in their skins for 20 minutes, cool, peel and dice.
Boil the egg for 10 minutes, cool in cold water, peel and chop.
Mix with the yoghurt and finely chopped dill.
Serve immediately; keep in the fridge for no more than 1 day.
Don't leave yoghurt salad at room temperature for more than 1 hour.
Wash and drain the bulgur.
Dice the pepper, courgette and tomato small.
Put the vegetables, bulgur, olive oil and hot water in an ovenproof dish and mix.
Cover tightly with foil and bake for 30 minutes until the bulgur has absorbed the water.
Beware of steam when removing the foil; rest for 10 minutes and serve.
Boil the turkey breast, let it cool and slice thinly.
Wash and dry the lettuce.
Spread yoghurt on the bread; add the turkey and lettuce and close.
Use home-boiled turkey instead of deli turkey; ready-made versions contain a lot of salt and additives.
Preheat the oven to 120°C; line the tray with baking paper.
Wash the apples; remove the core and cut into 3 mm rings.
Arrange the rings on the tray without overlapping and sprinkle with cinnamon.
Bake for 90 minutes; turn at 45 minutes.
Turn off the oven and let the rings cool inside with the door ajar; they dry and become crisp.
Dried apple can be hard and chewy; give it to young children in small pieces, sitting down.
Keep in a closed jar for 1 week.
Finely shred the boiled chicken; seed the pepper and chop finely.
Spread the chicken, pepper and cheese over the flatbread.
Roll up tightly and place seam side down on the tray.
Bake for 8 minutes until the cheese melts and the flatbread is lightly golden.
Wash and grate the tomatoes; discard the skins.
Melt the butter in a pan and toast the flour for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the tomato and stir for 2 minutes.
Add the water slowly, stirring so it doesn't go lumpy.
Serve sprinkled with a little grated cheese.
Dice the courgette and carrot small.
Soften the vegetables in a pan with 1 spoonful of olive oil for 5 minutes.
Add the tomato sauce and drained pasta and mix.
Cook the meatballs in a griddle pan over medium heat for 4 minutes on each side.
Mix the boiled beans with olive oil and finely chopped parsley; mash the beans lightly.
Arrange the meatballs and bean salad on the plate.
Cut the meatballs into small pieces and serve.
Add the oats, finely chopped raisins and cinnamon and mix; leave for 5 minutes.
Cool completely in the dish, then cut into bars.
Dice the chicken and marinate with the yoghurt in the fridge for 30 minutes.
Cut the pepper and courgette to the same size as the chicken.
Thread the chicken and vegetables alternately onto skewers and place on the tray.
Remove all the pieces from the skewers before giving to the child.
Break into small pieces and serve.
Soak the white cheese in water for 1 hour to remove salt.
Mash the boiled potato and cheese with a fork and mix.
Whisk the milk and egg; set aside 2 spoonfuls for the top.
Lay out the filo sheet and moisten with the sauce; place the filling along one edge and roll up.
Arrange the rolls on the tray and brush with the reserved sauce.
Bake for 30 minutes until golden on top.
Finely grate the carrot and squeeze out the liquid.
Mix the cooked quinoa, carrot, egg and breadcrumbs; leave for 10 minutes.
Peel the potatoes and cut into finger-thick sticks.
Toss with olive oil and arrange on the tray; bake for 15 minutes.
Add the sea bass to the tray; bake for 15 more minutes.
Drizzle with the lemon and flake the fish; serve lukewarm with the potatoes.
Melt the butter in a pan and stir the spinach for 2 minutes.
Add the rice and toast for 1 minute; add the water.
When it boils, cook covered over low heat for 15 minutes until the water is absorbed.
Wash the fruit; peel and dice the apple and banana small.
Cut the grapes lengthways into quarters.
Put the fruit in a bowl.
Serve immediately; apple and banana turn brown.
Knead the mince, grated tomato and finely chopped parsley well; then wash your hands.
Spread the mixture very thinly over the flatbread; a thick layer may not cook through.
Bake for 10 minutes until the mince is fully cooked and the edges are golden.
Don't add chilli; let cool and slice.
Preheat the oven to 180°C; grease a muffin tin or use paper cases.
Whisk the carrot, egg, orange juice and honey.
Dice the chicken, potato, carrot, pepper and tomato; cut the vegetables smaller than the chicken.
Put everything into the clay pot and add half a glass of water.
Put the clay pot into a cold oven; bake at 190°C for 45 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 190°C; grease a small loaf tin.
Whisk the egg and yoghurt.
Add the cornmeal, flour and baking powder and mix just until combined; add the cheese.
